chapter: The band, its players and singers
title: Hiring bassist John Clayton on Ray Brown's word
summary: Basie hired John Clayton on Ray Brown's recommendation without hearing him, and says a bass feature at Westbury was made up on the spot.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well, on what basis do you hire -- like you just hired a bass player, right. John Clinton.
Okay, why did you hire him?
I hired -- why I -- because he was recommended to me by I think one of the great bass players in the world, was Ray Brown -- he's a student of Ray Brown and Ray said here's a guy you should try.
And you tried him -- did you listen to him before you hired him.

No, just on the basis of Ray, because Ray knows me and I knew he had been studying and he was one of Ray's pupils and he was there, something anyway, if it didn't fit me, but I just like him. He fits the rhythm section and fits the band, I think, and I think after we work together after awhile, we'll become a team.
He sounds great for the band, in fact it's almost like he's featured, the bass is featured the way you have it at Westbury.
It's just a little fill in. We just made that up.
Right on there, you mean, it hadn't been rehearsed or anything. Did you do it in Philadelphia?
You say we just made it up.
Yeah, say give me a chord at the end, and that's all.
